WHEN ENGINEERING BECOMES ALPHA
Why elite HFT firms are competing for the engineers behind the edge.

One of the industry’s most influential technology Designer and Founder of C++ recently joined one of the world’s leading high frequency trading firms.

And that says a lot about where the market is heading.

In HFT, technology isn’t infrastructure sitting behind the business.

It is part of the edge.

Microseconds matter. CPU architecture matters. Memory, networking, concurrency and system design matter.

Which is why the talent bar is changing.

The industry isn’t just looking for engineers who can write C++.

It wants engineers who understand what happens after the code compiles.

Where is the bottleneck?
Where can latency be eliminated?
How much more performance can be extracted from the same hardware?

At the highest level of trading, these aren’t simply engineering problems.

They can become competitive advantages.

For engineers, this makes deep expertise in C++, low-latency systems, OS internals, networking, and hardware increasingly valuable, particularly when paired with quantitative thinking.

At Emaago, we see this as one of the clearest signals in the market:

The best trading firms are competing for the best engineers, because engineering is becoming the edge.
